pr_title: roachtest: Add LDAP conn. latency test via roachtest
pr_body:
No test previously existed to compute and monitor LDAP
connection latency

Created a roachtest which leverages the workload
to get the stats for LDAP connection latency
The test provisions an openLDAP service and it's user `jdoe`
which is authenticated on the CRDB via LDAP.
The test
* provisions openLDAP with TLS connection
* Creates a user named jdoe into CRDB
* Sets the HBA conf and custom CA into the cluster settings
* runs the workload binary to compute the connection latency

Epic: [CRDB-40412](https://cockroachlabs.atlassian.net/browse/CRDB-40412)
Fixes: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/127358

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/130998)

issue_context.title: ldap: scalability & performance testing
issue_context.body:
### Performance - Connection Latency
We should measure the latency of each connection to CRDB server in the context of LDAP authN/authZ, and derive stats like avg, p90, p95, etc.

Authentication latency should not exceed Round Trip Time to the LDAP/AD server + 10 ms.
Authorization latency should not exceed Round Trip Time + 500ms.
Excluding round trip time to the LDAP server we should target sub 1 second latency when authenticating and authorizing a user.


### Scalability - Concurrent Connections
We should scale test our LDAP implementation to ensure it can keep up with a large number of connections being established. 

LDAP/AD authentication should be able to sustain 2500 connections per second on a 3 node cluster with 4 vCPUs per node.

Microsoft AD Server has 5000 concurrent connections as the default ([see link](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/active-directory/view-set-ldap-policy-using-ntdsutil)), we should be able to sustain at least 50% of that number or 2500 connections.

Ideally we should do this in a roachtest that measures LDAP/AD authentication performance on a nightly basis against a LDAP/AD server in CI/CD.

Jira issue: CRDB-40412

Epic CRDB-33829

```
func setClusterSetting(ctx context.Context, t test.Test, conn *pgx.Conn, setting, value string) {
	_, err := conn.ExecContext(ctx, fmt.Sprintf("SET CLUSTER SETTING %s='%s'", setting, value))
	require.NoError(t, err)
}
```

The `SET CLUSTER SETTING` statements could also go through this function.
